FOOT SYMPTOMS
Check if problem is in the joint: ask patient to walk, sit and stand up with arms folded. If unable to do all actions comfortably and problem seems to be specifically in the joint 77.

If the patient has diabetes or PVD, identify the foot at risk and review more frequently if patient also has any of: • Skin: callus, corns, cracks, wet soft skin between toes 85, ulcers 90. • Foot deformity: most commonly bunions (see above). If foot deformity, refer for specialist care. • Sensation: light prick sensation abnormal after 2 attempts. • Circulation: absent or reduced foot pulses.

Advise patient with diabetes or PVD to care for feet daily to prevent ulcers and amputation • Inspect and wash feet daily and carefully dry between the toes. Avoid soaking feet. • Moisten dry cracked feet daily with emulsifying ointment (UE), avoid area between toes. • If cuts/blisters/sores, keep wound clean and return to clinic if not healing.

• Avoid walking barefoot or wearing shoes without socks. Change socks/stockings daily. Inspect inside shoes daily. • Clip nails straight, file sharp edges. Avoid cutting corns/calluses or using chemicals/plasters to remove them. • Avoid testing water temperature with feet or using hot water bottles or heaters near feet.

Approach to the patient with foot symptoms not needing urgent attention If cracks/peeling/scaly lesions between toes or thickened scaly skin on soles/heels/sides of feet, tinea pedis (athlete's foot) likely 81.
Generalised foot pain
Constant burning pain, pins/needles or numbness of feet worse at night

Peripheral neuropathy likely • Test for HIV 124 and syphilis 66. If HIV positive, give routine care 126. • Check for diabetes 19. • In the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks1/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription or over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165. If harmful alcohol use, give thiamine 100mg daily. • Give amitriptyline2 25mg (10mg if ≥ 65 years) at night. If needed, increase by 25mg (10mg if ≥ 65 years) every 2 weeks, up to 75mg at night. • If on isoniazid, increase pyridoxine to 50mg 8 hourly for 3 weeks, then give 50mg daily. If pregnant, discuss/refer. • If on linezolid, check RR-TB treatment duration and discuss with TB expert/helpline 200. • If one-sided, weakness or severe numbness, refer same week. • If patient known to have cancer, refer same day. • If available, refer to physiotherapist. • If no better with treatment, discuss/refer.

Bunion likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) for up to 5 days. • If severe pain or ulcer, refer.

Plantar fasciitis likely • Advise to: decrease aggravating physical activity (like running). Apply ice. Avoid bare feet - wear shoes with good support or use shoe inserts. Stretch and exercise feet regularly: stretch calf muscle/s on waking and before sleep, roll foot/feet over cold drink bottle. • If BMI3 ≥ 25, assess and advise 156. • Give as needed: paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) or ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for up to 5 days (avoid ibuprofen if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant). • Refer for physiotherapy, if available.
1One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/bottle (330mL) of beer. 2Avoid if on RR-TB treatment. 3BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m) ÷ height (m).
